- P-173 **A numeral converts where it stands: where its place fixes a type, into that type at compile time from its exact value; where nothing fixes one, into the machine default, a `ZZ32`, or a `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit, and with a radix point an `RR64`.** A place fixes a type when its declared type has a coercion from the numeral type, as the eight number types have and a program's own type may (P-174); `Any`, `Object`, `Number`, an unbounded type parameter and no declared type take the default. So `x = 3` is a `ZZ32`, and `x SEQV z` is `true` for `z: ZZ32 = 3`; `bigN = 3000000000` is a `ZZ64` at its binding (row 946). The default applies to a numeral, a literal after the fold, never to an expression of a numeral type, and a `nat` parameter used as a value is a `ZZ32` where it is a size (P-40), and, where it is one of a numeral type's four numbers, converts where it stands, a `ZZ` where nothing fixes a type (P-174). A type parameter that several numerals fix takes the narrowest default that holds every value, an `RR64` where any has a radix point, each numeral converting into it exactly; a float numeral whose conversions into `QQ` and `RR64` tie reads `RR64`. At a typed place the conversion is exact or rounds once (P-76, P-172), and a numeral outside the type's range is refused statically; walk converts from the exact value at the same places, place by place, before it runs the checker (P-12). An expression of numerals alone folds exactly before the checker into a signed constant, which defaults as an integer numeral, as a `QQ` for a quotient, or as an `RR64` with a radix point: so `x = 7/2` is a `QQ`, `1/2 = 0.5` is `true`, and `-2147483648`, prefix minus on a numeral, folded, is a `ZZ32`. `gg(5, w)`, with `gg` declared at `(ZZ32, T)` and at `(Any, Any)`, runs the `ZZ32` declaration (P-49). The parameter types of the declaration that a call runs are places that fix a type, and a numeral argument goes to the most specific declaration that takes it, by its own conversion if need be, with its default as the last resort: `u = 0` is `true` for `u: NN32 = 0`, the numeral an `NN32` at `NN32`'s own `=` (P-46 gives the rule and its ground; row 1016 holds where walk departs, and row 1017 where both paths do). Why: the design completes the Working Draft's, whose numerals have types of their own so that a library decides by coercions how they meet other types (P-174 gives that ground). It bends P-26 in two places, the numeral types, whose names and static parameters are the Draft's (P-174), and the places that fix no type, where the compiler's prelude, the team's later word, keeps the numeral's own type; the curator takes the bend by his right to finish the specification. He declined exact defaults, `ZZ` and `QQ` (the 2012 restart gives `NN` and `QQ`, `literals.tick:25`), since microGPT's untyped hyperparameters (`MicroGptFlat.fss:18`) would then be rationals and every untyped index would need `asZZ32`. - F-341 **Walk's numeral is its default, carrying the numeral's four numbers, and converts from them where its place fixes a type.** An integer numeral is a `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, a radix-point numeral the `RR64` nearest its value, one value per site (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Numerals.java`). At a typed binding, an assignment, a field, a parameter, a declared return type and a coercion it converts through the place type's coercion from `NaturalNumeral` or `RadixPointNumeral`, run with the four numbers bound as values of type `ZZ`, one result per site and type; a folded constant at a library number type converts from its exact value, outside the coercion; a numeral out of the type's range, one that rounds to an infinity at `RR32` or `RR64`, one at a type with no coercion from it, or one outside its coercion's `where` clause is refused there when it runs; a store keeps its default alone. Dispatch fits it at its default, unless its own coercion reaches a declaration strictly below, which then runs (F-366), else by its own type's coercions only, and reads a tie at the default; a type parameter that several numerals fix takes the narrowest default holding them all. # Rung N: a numeral coercion's four numbers convert where they stand (P-174)

- problem: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-36/probes/fixes-36.md:14` (walk stops at `Byte(v)`, 'Unification error: Closure/Constructor for Byte param 1 ($b:ZZ32) got arg 200:ZZ of type ZZ') and `:28` (compiled, 'ZZ32->Byte is not applicable to an argument of type ZZ.'); the getters on the four numbers counted at `:79`.

## What changed and why

P-174: "A coercion's body is a computation at compile time, with no method invocation: a number used as a value there converts where it stands, as a numeral does (P-173), into the type that its place fixes, and is refused statically where it does not fit ... where nothing fixes a type, it is an exact integer, `ZZ`." Fork N1 builds it on both paths, fork N2 writes the coercions so.

**Walk** (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Numerals.java`). `convert` bound each of the four numbers as an `FBigNum`. It now binds each as a number (`number`, `:123`): a numeral value of kind `STATIC` whose default is a `ZZ` whatever its value (`Site(BigInteger)`, `:104`, flag `number`). Walk's numeral machinery then converts it where its place fixes a type, as it converts a folded constant: at a library number type from its exact value (`exactAt`, through `Coercions.numeralCoercionFor`'s range check, so a number outside the type's range finds no coercion and the place stops with walk's message for the place, as 'got arg 3000000000:ZZ of type ZZ'); at a program's type through that type's coercion from `ZZ`; where nothing fixes a type it is its default, a `ZZ` (`w = v` binds an `FBigNum`). A number that the body returns as it is converts at the coercion's result type (`:555`, `atReturn`), so `ZZ32`'s coercion is `= v`. The dispatch cache does not hold whether a number fits a narrower type, since its default is a `ZZ` whatever its value, so a choice that converts a number at a library type is not cached (`ownCoercionFrom`, `:434`). At a call walk sends a number, as a numeral, to the most specific declaration that takes it, by its own conversion if need be (`OverloadedFunction.belowByNumerals`, unchanged).

**The checker** (`scala_src/typechecker/`). A number is still typed `ZZ` (`staticenv/KindEnv.scala:72-75`, `getType`, comment only). The owning checker tells the coercion oracle which expressions are numbers: a reference to an exact static parameter that no variable hides (`STypeChecker.scala:184`). Where a place fixes `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `RR64` or `RR32` of the library, `buildCoercion` converts the number there, as the reference typed at that type (`CoercionOracle.scala:211`, `NumeralConversion.numberAt`, `:601`, `numberTarget`, `:587`), also as an element of a tuple at a tuple type (`:198`); into `QQ` it goes by `QQ`'s coercion from `ZZ`, which exists, and at a program's type by that type's coercion from `ZZ`, as a folded constant does. Such a conversion ranks as a coercion that the call needs (`counts`, `:575`). At a call, `Functionals.typedApplication` (`:888`, outside `typedApplicationOfChecked`) first resolves the call in a try checker with the numbers read as `ZZ` (`NumeralConversion.numbersAsZZ`, `:581`), and converts them only where no declaration takes them so: `v / r^m` keeps `ZZ`'s `^` and `/`, `Byte(v)` and `numeralRR64(v, r, 0)` convert. Once every declaration of a component is checked, `NumeralConversion.numberRefusals` (`:686`, called from `impls/Decls.scala:85`) reads each written numeral that the component converts into a program's type by that type's numeral coercion of the same component, finds where that coercion's checked body converts each number into a bounded number type (`numberUses`, `:737`), and refuses, at the numeral's place, a number that does not fit: 'The numeral 3000000000 gives the coercion to Wide the number v = 3000000000, which is out of range for ZZ32, whose values are -2147483648 to 2147483647.' A numeral at a library type is range-checked as before (`outOfRange`), and the library's own bodies take no refusal.

**The code generator.** A numeral coercion's method keeps its parameters, the four numbers as `ZZ` values (`CodeGen.numeralCoercionMethods`). A reference to such a parameter that the checker typed at a bounded number type converts the `ZZ` on the stack (`CodeGen.java:7136`, `convertNumber`, `:8508`) by a method of the `ZZ` payload, `FZZ.numberAsZZ32`, `numberAsZZ64`, `numberAsNN32`, `numberAsNN64`, `numberAsRR64` or `numberAsRR32` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ.java:50-73`), then the type's `make`; an integer conversion raises `IntegerOverflow` where the number does not fit, a float one rounds once. The fold reads the same typing: a number typed at a built-in type is that type's representation (`NumeralCoercionFold.java:233`), so `ZZ32`'s `= v` still folds into an `int` constant.

**The coercions** (fork N2). The one library: `RR64`'s two (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:388-389`, `numeralRR64(v, r, 0)` and `numeralRR64(v, r, m)`), `QQ`'s radix-point one (`:635`, `v / r^m`), `ZZ32`'s, `ZZ64`'s and `NN64`'s (`:847`, `:954`, `:1065`, each `= v`); and `FortressBuiltin`'s three, which the brief's file list does not name but fork N2's "the one library" covers (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:67-68`, `RR32`'s `numeralRR32(v, r, 0)` and `numeralRR32(v, r, m)`; `:263`, `NN32`'s `= v`). `AnyIntegral`'s coercion (`FortressLibrary.fss:743-748`) binds `z = v` and calls `z.asZZ32` on that `ZZ` variable, not on a number, and stays. === tests/NumeralCoercionBodyWalk.fss
(* A numeral coercion's four numbers, used as values in its body, convert where they stand, with no getter: v at a ZZ32 or an RR64 parameter, n at a ZZ32 parameter, and v where nothing fixes a type an exact ZZ (literals.tex, section "Literals"). *)
component NumeralCoercionBodyWalk
export Executable

value object Byte(b: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) where { v < 256 } = Byte(v)
end

value object Digits(count: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) = Digits(n)
end

value object Approx(a: RR64)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Approx(v)
end

value object Big(z: ZZ)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = do
        w = v
        Big(w)
    end
end

run(): () = do
    y: Byte = 200
    assert(y.b, 200, "v converts into ZZ32 at Byte's parameter")
    d: Digits = 00.5
    assert(d.count, 3, "n converts into ZZ32 at Digits' parameter")
    p: Approx = 9007199254740993
    assert(p.a, 9007199254740992.0, "v converts into RR64 at Approx's parameter, rounded once")
    g: Big = 123456789012345678901234567890
    assert(g.z, 123456789012345678901234567890, "v, bound where nothing fixes a type, is an exact ZZ")
    println("PASS")
end

end
=== tests/NumeralCoercionNumberAtCallWalk.fss
(* A numeral coercion's number at a call goes, as a numeral does, to the most specific declaration that takes it, by its own conversion if need be: tag(x: ZZ32) beside tag(x: Number) runs tag(ZZ32), and a call that only a conversion reaches converts it (literals.tex, section "Literals"). *)
component NumeralCoercionNumberAtCallWalk
export Executable

tag(x: Number): ZZ32 = 1
tag(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 2

only(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 3

value object Tagged(t: ZZ32, u: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Tagged(tag(v), only(v))
end

run(): () = do
    k: Tagged = 7
    assert(k.u, 3, "v at only converts into ZZ32")
    assert(k.t, 2, "v at tag runs tag(ZZ32), which its conversion reaches, below tag(Number)")
    println("PASS")
end

end
=== tests/NumeralCoercionNumberRangeWalk.fss
(* A numeral coercion's number that does not fit the place where its body uses it is refused where the numeral's place runs: v of 3000000000 at a ZZ32 parameter. *)
component NumeralCoercionNumberRangeWalk
export Executable

value object Wide(w: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Wide(v)
end

fits: Wide = 5
tooWide: Wide = 3000000000

run() = println("FAIL: 3000000000 at a coercion whose body puts v at a ZZ32 parameter was accepted")

end

load_exception_contains=param 1 ($w:ZZ32) got arg 3000000000

component NumeralCoercionBodyWalk
export Executable

value object Byte(b: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) where { v < 256 } = Byte(v)
end

value object Digits(count: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) = Digits(n)
end

value object Approx(a: RR64)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Approx(v)
end

value object Big(z: ZZ)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = do
        w = v
        Big(w)
    end
end

run(): () = do

    g: Big = 123456789012345678901234567890

    println("PASS")
end

end

 with one rounding into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}; that the

@@ -5435,8 +5435,9 @@ A signed constant at a number type of \library\ is converted from its exact

-type at the place's first evaluation, with the four numbers bound as values of
-type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, and keeps its result for the place; it refuses a numeral
+type at the place's first evaluation, with the four numbers bound as numbers

 only when the place is evaluated: one outside an integer type's range, one

@@ -5766,6 +5767,75 @@ For example, ``\txt{foo}''\EXP{\|}''\txt{bar}'' yields ``\txt{foobar}''.
 \item[Route C] The same under route~C.
 \end{description}
 
+\subsection{The four numbers in a numeral coercion's body}
+\seclabel{revival-numeral-numbers}
+
+\begin{description}
+\item[Affected sections] \secref{literals}; \secref{natparams};
+\secref{revival-numerals}.
+\item[Change] \secref{literals} says that a coercion from a numeral type
+computes the type's value from the four numbers with no method invocation; that
+each of the four, used as a value in the coercion's body, is converted where it
+stands, as a numeral is, into the type that its place fixes, from its exact
+value, and is an integer of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} where nothing fixes a type;
+and that a number that does not fit the type that its place fixes, at a
+numeral's four numbers, is a static error at that numeral's place.
+It gives \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s coercion, \EXP{v}, and a byte type's,
+\EXP{\TYP{Byte}(v)}, as examples, with a box.
+The box of \secref{natparams} on the four numbers says the same, and three
+sentences of \secref{revival-numerals} that read the four as values of type
+\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} point here.
+\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; the revival decided
+on 23~November 2026 that a coercion's body is a computation at compile time with
+no method invocation, in which a number used as a value converts where it
+stands, as a numeral does, into the type that its place fixes, is refused
+statically where it does not fit, and is an exact integer, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}},
+where nothing fixes a type.
+The revival's text of 9~November 2026 read the four as values of type
+\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} wherever they stand, so that \library's coercions and those of
+the revival's tests converted each by a method, as \EXP{v.\VAR{asZZ32}}, though
+the four numbers are static parameters, not values with methods.
+A reversal would read the four as values of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} wherever they
+stand again, and would put a method back in each coercion that needs one of
+them at another type.
+\item[Effect] Both implementations convert each of the four numbers where it
+stands, and \library's coercions, the compiled path's own library's and the
+revival's tests' are written with no method on the four numbers, as
+\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s \EXP{v}.
+The compiled type checker types a number as \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, converts it where
+its place fixes \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32},
+\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, and refuses, at the
+numeral's place, a number that does not fit there, where the coercion is
+declared in the numeral's component; the compiled code converts the number from
+the \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} that holds it, and the compiled coercion of another
+component raises \TYP{IntegerOverflow} when the class that holds the numeral's
+place is initialized, where such a number does not fit (row~NEW-N-1 of the
+revival's gap ledger).
+The interpreter binds each number as a value of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} that
+converts where its place fixes a type, as a numeral does, and refuses one that
+does not fit when the place is evaluated.
+At a call, the interpreter sends a number, as a numeral, to the most specific
+declaration that takes it, by its own conversion if need be
+(\secref{resolving-coercion}); the compiled type checker, which checks the body
+once for every numeral, reads a number at a call as a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} where a
+declaration of the called name takes one, and converts it only where none does,
+so that on the compiled path a declaration more specific than the one that takes
+the \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, which the number's conversion reaches, does not run
+(row~NEW-N-2).
+\item[Original text] None: the Working Draft does not say how a coercion's body
+reads the static parameters of a numeral type.
+The passage that this change builds stands, in
+\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines
+142--145:
+\begin{quote}
+This approach allows library designers to decide how numerals should
+interact with other types of objects by defining coercion operations
+(see \secref{coercion} for an explanation of coercion
+in Fortress).
+\end{quote}
+\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
+\end{description}
+
 \subsection{The programming environment of the overview}
 \seclabel{revival-environment}

3812:- P-168 **What `SEQV` means, on both paths: the specification's rule, with no special case for any type but the numeral types.** Values of different types are never strictly equivalent; two value objects of one type are when their fields are, tuples element by element and floats by their bit patterns; two reference objects are only when they are one object (`Specification/basic/objects.tex`, "Object Equivalence" and "Value Objects"). The one exception: two values of a numeral type, which exist only inside a coercion's body, are strictly equivalent when their reduced values are equal, so `2.5` and `2.50` are there (P-174). Both paths read the `value` modifier. Each path changes its own code: walk drops its equivalence across types (row 909) and its answer `true` for value objects whose body declares no field (row 113); the compiled helper `equality.sEquiv` gains the rule for value objects, tuples and floats (rows 906 and 907; the prelude's own `===` keeps row 908 until the switch-over). `ZZ`'s and `QQ`'s values are value objects (P-166). Strings are reference objects: the library declares `FlatString`, `CatString` and `SubString` without `value`, so two such strings are strictly equivalent only when they are one object, and text equality is the strings' own `=`; P-171 makes two literals of one text one object. This overrules the team's code on both paths, walk's `seqv` and the prelude's `opr ===(a:String, b:String) = a=b`, where the specification is silent on strings. A program with a `value object CC64` tests it on both paths beside the review's 14 cases (F-326). Why: the specification's rule read as written, over the team's unfinished code of 2008 and 2010, which its authors called preliminary and incomplete; P-167 makes this one comparison that both paths answer. Detail: `reviews/any-carrier-2026-11-06.md`, section 2.4; `reviews/string-equivalence-2026-11-06.md`, sections 3 and 7.
3820:### P-174
3828:- P-172 **A numeral with a radix point has the Working Draft's type `RadixPointNumeral` (P-174), which holds the numeral's exact value: `QQ` converts from it exactly, and `RR64` and `RR32` with one rounding.** So `3.125` converts to the `QQ` value `3125/1000`, `q: QQ = 0.5` binds and `1/2 = 0.5` is `true`; into `RR64` or `RR32` a numeral rounds once, to the type's nearest value, on both paths (row 862: the compiled path rounds two or three times). `QQ`, `RR64` and `RR32` each declare the pair of `=` that goes with each coercion (P-165). Where nothing fixes a type the numeral is an `RR64` (P-173): `Cell(0.5)` is a `Cell[\RR64\]`, and a bare numeral prints as that double, so `"" 2.50` is `"2.5"`, and the team's `tests/NumberPrintTest.fss:16`, which asserts that a numeral prints as written, changes. `RadixPointNumeral` stands beside the number types, as the compiler's prelude declares its `FloatLiteral` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:996`), in place of the interpreter library's `value object FloatLiteral extends RR64` (`FortressBuiltin.fsi:44`). Walk converts such a numeral from its exact value where its place fixes a type, at a binding, a parameter and a field, so `y: RR64 = 0.5` is `SEQV` a computed `0.25 + 0.25`. The specification's literals chapter and the coercions of `basic-lib/numbers.tex:43` follow, with an Appendix I entry, in the revision form (P-96). Not decided here: `round` of a numeral within half an ulp of a tie, which rounds the numeral's nearest double, not the rational (row 360). No line of microGPT changes, and by reading its numerals keep their bits. Why: the Working Draft keeps a numeral unconverted, since "converting it immediately to a floating-point number may lose precision", gives 3.125 "the rational value 3125/1000", has the library coerce a compound numeral to the rationals, and converts a static rational expression into a float with "at most one floating-point rounding error" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-173`); the curator reads it so: nothing is lost in `QQ`, and a float of fixed size takes one rounding.

<!-- The decision record of climb batch 36's rung N: the specification's passages that read a numeral coercion's four numbers as values of type ZZ wherever they stand, brought in line with P-174, each with its original, its new text, the reason and the way back. -->
# Rung N: the four numbers in a numeral coercion's body, the decision record

The decision is the curator's, P-174 as it stands since 23 November 2026: "A coercion's body is a computation at compile time, with no method invocation: a number used as a value there converts where it stands, as a numeral does (P-173), into the type that its place fixes, and is refused statically where it does not fit ... where nothing fixes a type, it is an exact integer, `ZZ`." Fork N1 of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-36.md`, section 3, gives its default on both paths. Every passage below is the revival's own text of 9 November 2026, not the Working Draft's: the Draft does not say how a coercion's body reads a numeral type's static parameters, so each passage's original is the base's text (`b5a758846d`), and Appendix I's new entry quotes the Draft's sentence that the design builds (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:142-145`).

## 1. The literals chapter (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex`, section "Literals")

Original, `literals.tex:186-188` at the base:

```latex
The parameter of such a coercion has no value: its body computes the type's
value from the four numbers, which it reads as values, integers of type
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\secref{natparams}).
```

New text, `literals.tex:186-205`: the body computes the type's value "with no method invocation"; each of the four, used as a value in the body, "is converted where it stands, as a numeral is: into the type that its place fixes, from its exact value; where nothing fixes a type, it is an integer of type ZZ"; a number that does not fit the type its place fixes, at a numeral's four numbers, "is a static error at that numeral's place, as a numeral out of the range of its place's type is"; ZZ32's coercion is `= v` and a byte type's `where { v < 256 } = Byte(v)`; and the box `\revision{revival-numeral-numbers}`.

Reason: P-174's sentence above; the old sentence made the one library's coercions and seventeen tests convert each number by a getter, `v.asZZ32`, which the curator refused on 23 November 2026 (P-174's history, the block of 14:33Z: "No method invocations").

Way back: restore the three lines above and the getters in the coercions (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `CompilerBuiltin.fss` and the tests), and the checker's, walk's and the code generator's reading of each number as a `ZZ` wherever it stands.

## 2. The box on a nat parameter used as a value (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex`, section "Nat and Int Parameters")

Original, `trait-parameters.tex:115-118` at the base:

```latex
The revival decided on 9~November 2026 that the four numbers of a numeral
type (\secref{literals}) are \KWD{nat} parameters of any size, which, read as
values in the body of a coercion from that type, are integers of type
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}}: the bound of a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter to the range
```

New text, `trait-parameters.tex:115-120`: "are \KWD{nat} parameters of any size, and on 23~November 2026 that, used as values in the body of a coercion from that type, they are converted where they stand, as a numeral is, and are integers of type ZZ where nothing fixes a type (\secref{revival-numeral-numbers}): the bound of ...", the rest of the box unchanged.

Reason and way back: as in 1.

## 3. Appendix I (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`)

Three sentences of the entry `revival-numerals` read the four numbers as values of type `ZZ`; each now points to the new entry:

- The Change, `changes.tex:5202-5205` at the base, "whose body computes the type's value from the four numbers, read as values of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}: exactly into ...", now "... from the four numbers, each converted where it stands (\secref{revival-numeral-numbers}): exactly into ...".
- The Change, `changes.tex:5255-5257` at the base, "the four numbers of a numeral type, which are integers of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} in a coercion's body", now "which in a coercion's body are converted where they stand (\secref{revival-numeral-numbers})".
- The Effect, `changes.tex:5437-5439` at the base, the interpreter "with the four numbers bound as values of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}", now "bound as numbers that convert where they stand (\secref{revival-numeral-numbers})".

The new entry, `\subsection{The four numbers in a numeral coercion's body}`, `\seclabel{revival-numeral-numbers}`, before "The programming environment of the overview", gives the affected sections, the change, its rationale (P-174's decision of 23 November 2026, and the reversal), the effect with the two departures that the change leaves (rows NEW-N-1 and NEW-N-2 of the gap ledger, which the gather numbers), the Draft's sentence that it builds, and route C.

Reason and way back: as in 1; the way back also deletes the new entry and restores the three sentences.

## 4. What the passages do not settle, and the reading built

At a call, the text sends a number, "as a numeral is", to the declaration that the call runs, and P-173 sends a numeral to the most specific declaration that takes it, by its own conversion if need be. Walk does so at each run. The compiled checker checks a coercion's body once for every numeral, so it cannot know whether a number's conversion reaches a more specific declaration: it reads a number at a call as a `ZZ` where a declaration takes one, and converts it only where none does (`Functionals.typedApplication`). The new entry's Effect names this departure (row NEW-N-2); the report puts it to the curator.

value object Clamped(b: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Clamped(if v < 100 then do v end else 99 end)
end

value object Chosen(b: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = do
        c: ZZ32 = case n of 3 => v; else => 0 end
        Chosen(if v < 1000 then c else v end)
    end
end

value object Wide64(w: ZZ64)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = do
        z: ZZ32 = 5
        Wide64(if v < 100 then v else z end)
    end
end

value object Big(z: ZZ)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = do
        w = v
        Big(w)
    end
end
    assert(p.a = 9007199254740992.0, "v converts into RR64 at Approx's parameter, rounded once")
    c1: Clamped = 42
    assert(c1.b, 42, "v converts in a do block in an if's branch at Clamped's parameter")
    c2: Clamped = 123
    assert(c2.b, 99, "the if's other branch, a numeral, converts at Clamped's parameter")
    c3: Chosen = 123
    assert(c3.b, 123, "v converts in a case's branch at a ZZ32 binding")
    c4: Chosen = 5000
    assert(c4.b, 5000, "v converts in an if's branch beside a ZZ32 variable at Chosen's parameter")
    c5: Wide64 = 42
    assert(c5.w = 42, "v converts in an if's branch beside a ZZ32 variable, which coerces, at Wide64's parameter")
    c6: Wide64 = 500
    assert(c6.w = 5, "the ZZ32 variable in the if's other branch coerces at Wide64's parameter")
    g: Big = 123456789012345678901234567890
    assert(g.z.asString, "123456789012345678901234567890", "v, bound where nothing fixes a type, is an exact ZZ")

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

(* A numeral at a place whose type names a type parameter of its generic declaration is one value for each instance: two evaluations at one instance's type are one object, two instances' types two objects. *)
component XXXNumeralGenericPlaceCompiled
export Executable

object Gen[\T\](v: ZZ32)
  coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Gen[\T\](v)
end

object Box[\T\]()
  m(): Gen[\T\] = 3
end

sEq(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")

run(): () = do
  a = Box[\RR64\]()
  b = Box[\String\]()
  assert(a.m().v, 3, "m() of Box of RR64 sees the value 3")
  assert(NOT sEq(a.m(), b.m()), "two instances' types give two objects")
  println("REACHED")
  assert(sEq(a.m(), a.m()), "two evaluations at one instance's type are one object")
  println("PASS")
end

end
